summary: Every character position can affect the displacement sum, establishing a linear input-inspection lower bound, while the legal distinct-letter domain ends at 26 and cannot support an honest runtime-scaling comparison.

optimality.argument: A correct algorithm must determine the destination of every character: swapping an unread pair in t preserves the permutation contract but can change the total. The accepted implementation indexes t once and processes each character of s once, matching that lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: Two unread positions in t can be swapped while preserving all source constraints and changing one or both absolute displacements.
The reference builds one position entry per character and performs one constant expected-time lookup and addition per character.
Regression checks every permutation through length nine and 100,000 deterministic random legal pairs through the maximum length against repeated independent index lookup.
Authored cases cover one character, identical strings, adjacent and endpoint swaps, reversals, rotations, and maximum-length permutations.
